deities: Bala Hanuman (child form of Lord Hanuman)

history.summary: The Bala Hanuman Temple stands on the southeastern bank of Lakhota Lake in Jamnagar and is dedicated to Hanuman in his youthful form, Bala Hanuman. It was established by Prem Bhikshuji (Prembhikshuji Maharaj) in 1963-64. Its global fame comes from the unbroken chanting of the Ram Naam mantra 'Shri Ram, Jai Ram, Jai Jai Ram' that began on 1 August 1964 and has continued 24 hours a day, in volunteer shifts, ever since - a feat recognised by the Guinness Book of World Records. The sanctum houses idols of Bala Hanuman alongside Rama, Sita and Lakshmana, with a framed photo of Prembhikshuji; the adjacent chanting hall is open to devotees who wish to join or sit in the continuous Ram Dhun.

town_description: Jamnagar is a coastal city in the Saurashtra region of Gujarat, on the Gulf of Kutch, founded in 1540 by Jam Rawal of the Jadeja Rajput clan as Nawanagar. Nicknamed 'Chhoti Kashi' (Little Kashi) for its many temples, it is a major pilgrim and tourist hub whose landmarks include Lakhota Lake, the Lakhota Palace museum and the Khijada (Navtanpuri) temple. The city is also an industrial centre, home to one of the world's largest oil refining complexes at nearby Motikhavdi.

travel.airport: Jamnagar Airport (JAI), about 10 km from the city centre (verify); well connected to Mumbai.
travel.railway: Jamnagar railway station on Western Railway, a few km from Lakhota Lake in the city centre (verify).
travel.road: Well connected by state highways and NH-27 to Rajkot (~90 km), Dwarka (~130 km) and Ahmedabad; local autos and taxis reach the lake.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for pleasant weather; evenings around aarti are the liveliest.
visitor_information.opening_hours: CONFLICT (verify): one directory lists 06:00-22:00, while several visitor reports say the temple is open 24x7. The Ram Naam chanting itself runs round the clock.
